design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller reports that Monday's executive dinner is off and asks for whatever pulling it
carries to be put on the account. He does not know, and the policy does not tell him, that the charge "is fixed only
after a cancellation entry stands against the order, carrying the value the order held when notice was given" - and
that the entry is his own to make, because only the client may pull their own order. The agent must read that out of
the charge policy, work out the value the order actually stands at (which is neither the 6400.00 it was quoted at nor
a simple sum, but the amendment entry's value under a free reduction band the agreement has earned, net of a discount
selected between two candidates and a concession earned on another product line), hand the registration to the client,
and only then work the charge on the entry the client's own write produced. Working the charge on the records as they
stand at the opening gives 1160.25 instead of 1409.29.

SCOPE. Already occupied by task 0: the billing of a served order and the settlement an agreement closes on, with the
invoicing and closure tools. Claimed here: the two problems catering_ext_client_cancellation_registration (tool register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0) and catering_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment (tool post_cancellation_charge_b7aa0639) - what an
order is worth when the client pulls it, and what the pulling costs. Nothing is reserved for a later task: with these
two the difficulty's four policies are complete and the two task scopes are disjoint in policy, tool, target write and
source of difficulty.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py on this difficulty, --task 1):
  {"task": 1, "key": "env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/catering_order_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
One prerequisite problem, and the two computations take five and four factors. The charge took 5; the registration
took 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root problem: catering_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment - the charge, the thing the caller asks to have put on the account.
  Prerequisite problem: catering_ext_client_cancellation_registration - the client's own registration of the cancellation.
  Edge root <- prerequisite: kind value_input, gate cancelled_value (a compute binding of the root), form state.
    Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the root policy's own rule:
    "The cancellation charge is fixed only after a cancellation entry stands against the order, carrying the value the order held when notice was given."
    Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result - the cancellation charge - to what it waits on with the
    ordering connective "only after", in the affirmative direction, and rewrites exactly into the negated "The
    cancellation charge is not fixed until a cancellation entry stands against the order, carrying the value the order
    held when notice was given" with no condition added, dropped or split. A charge is the kind of result this desk
    states in the affirmative - it is fixed only after what it rests on is in place - where the closing figure of task
    0's policy is stated in the negated direction, so the charter carries both. (2) Its waiting side is a
    record-visible state - a cancellation entry standing against the order and carrying a value - named in the words
    the order history uses; no action, performer or tool is named. (3) It carries no tool name, no policy id, no
    snake_case token and no row id. (4) Its strength is a hard requirement ("only after") over exactly the state the
    edge's condition names, no wider and no narrower.
    One-write proof for the state form: of the four writes this difficulty declares, only the registration produces a
    cancellation entry on a catering agreement; the invoicing write produces an invoice entry, the closure write
    produces no ledger entry, and the charge write produces a charge entry. A reader who sees that CO-726310 carries a
    placement and an amendment entry and nothing else, and reads the registration policy's own rule - which says what
    the value standing on an order at the moment notice is given comes to - has exactly one action open, and the
    charter reserves it to the client.
    Handling-time condition: a cancellation entry stands in the order history against the order reference, carrying
    the value the order held on the day notice was given. Resolving action: register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0, owner user.
    Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: CO-726310's only entries are the placement of 2026-03-28 and the
    amendment of 2026-04-10; the most recent cancellation entry on the agreement belongs to CO-723488 and was posted
    2026-01-16; the agreement's unsettled balance of 17812.50 contains nothing for CO-726310.
    Topological order: registration, then charge. Parallel edges: none.
    Deletion sensitivity (actually run): skipping the registration and replaying everything else gives 1160.25 rather
    than 1409.29.
  Customer's own write: the prerequisite problem's target tool register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0 is owner=user. The charter is explicit that
    only the client pulls their own order, and the act completes on the spot: the agent unlocks it, hands over the
    exact figure and wording, the client runs it himself, and the confirmation enters the shared transcript.
  user_scenario names no prerequisite problem: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint.
  The tool layer validates nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write subject catering_order_cancelled (the registration step). Governing base policy: catering_cancellation_charges.
  Gates whose applies_to covers that subject: cancellable_state only - registration_window applies to the charge
  subject alone. cancellable_state is a state gate, authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key
  catering_orders.order_reference bound to the action's order_reference; its state_contract admits an agreement
  standing active or on credit hold, and this one stands active. Its condition, "A cancellation charge is only raised against an order that has not been delivered; once an order is delivered the charge is a quality matter and is handled as a service credit instead.", holds because CO-726310 carries
  no delivery entry: the order was never served, so the matter is a cancellation and not a quality credit. No time gate
  applies to the registration.
  Write subject catering_cancellation_fee_posted (the charge step). Both gates of catering_cancellation_charges apply.
  cancellable_state is satisfied on the same grounds, with the order reference taken from the cancellation entry the
  preceding step wrote. registration_window is a time gate: clock frozen_time, anchor event "the day the client gives
  notice of the cancellation", anchor source catering_orders.notice_given_date, relation not_after, duration
  params.registration_window_hours (24), unit elapsed_hours, boundary inclusive, counting rule copied verbatim from
  base. The cancellation entry carries notice_given_date 2026-04-18 and the charge is raised at 09:15 on 2026-04-18, so
  nil elapsed hours have run against a 24-hour window. Boundary cases are recorded in
  solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility: notice on 2026-04-17 charged at 09:15 on 2026-04-18 is exactly 24 hours
  and inclusive, so in time; notice on 2026-04-16 would be 41 hours and out of time.
  Inherited item by item and not overridden: that a cancellation charge is only raised against an order that has not
  been delivered; that a cancellation is registered on the day notice is given; that a cancellation forced by Larkspur
  Table carries no charge whatever the notice (this one was forced by the client's own delegation, not by the kitchen);
  that an amendment which lowers order value is accepted whatever the credit position; and every eligibility boundary
  of catering_amendment_terms and catering_onboarding_terms not named in an overwrite. Overridden and declared clause by
  clause: on the charge policy, the base sentence measuring notice in whole hours to the service start time, replaced by
  the counting ladder, and the base sentence on the fourth cancellation in a rolling twelve months, replaced by the rate
  ladder; on the registration policy, the base sentence fixing the value the percentage applies to, replaced by the
  composition sentence, the base sentence on free-band repricing, replaced by the repricing ladder, and the base
  sentence on which standing discount governs, replaced by the discount selection ladder.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
  Registration step: the object is the single order CO-726310 under this agreement, keyed by order_reference, which
  its placement entry, its amendment entry and the cancellation entry written all carry. Rows that enter its value:
  its own placement entry (value and guest count) and its own amendment entry (value, guest count and notice day) -
  both the latest of their kind on the agreement, the placement of 2026-03-28 being later than every other placement
  and the amendment being the only one. Rows excluded: the five served orders, which carry delivery entries; the three
  earlier pulled orders CO-719780, CO-721644 and CO-723488, each of which already carries its own cancellation entry
  and its own charge on its own notice day.
  Charge step: the object is the cancellation entry the client has just registered against CO-726310. It is picked out
  as the latest cancellation entry by posting date, 2026-04-18, later than the three historical ones; its charge is
  written back against the same order reference, so the charge cannot attach to any of them. The aggregates it reads
  are scoped by window and event type, and each historical charge is already correlated to its own cancellation entry
  by order reference and notice day, so none is counted against this order.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  The five served orders (placement, delivery and invoice entries each) carry the delivery counts three factors rest
  on: five in the twelve months puts the free reduction band on its middle tier and the rebate on its middle tier, and
  three in the six months puts the discount selection on its top tier. Remove the deliveries of 2025-12-05, 2026-02-10
  and 2026-03-24 and the discount falls to the printed figure; drop the twelve-month count below three and both the
  band and the rebate fall away. The delivery of 2025-09-18 sits at seven months, just outside the six-month window -
  the near-miss a careless reader counts into the discount tier.
  The three pulled orders and their charges of 2990.00, 2275.00 and 2730.00 put the counting window on three charges
  and the registered count on four; all three sit inside twelve months and outside three, which is exactly what makes
  the counting-window factor bite.
  The three payments fix the unsettled balance of 17812.50 that decides the counting window, and the payment of
  2026-01-28 sits at two months so the three-month payment test is satisfied without deciding anything here.
  The order CO-726310 with its placement at 32 guests and its amendment to 30 is the prerequisite's own object: a
  reduction of 6.25 per cent, which sits between the printed 5.00 band and the earned 7.50 band and is the single fact
  that makes the band factor change the answer.
  The Seated Banquet Package billing under CA-22853 is the cross-difficulty evidence: it stands active and the largest
  guest count it handles is 350, which the banquet package schedule prints in its largest-guest-count column. It is
  joined to the catering agreement on the client account code, a field both records declare in the same CA- format, and
  its own venue is seeded VN-318 in the VN- format the banquet record declares.
  Remove it and the programme concession falls to nothing.
  Automatic clauses checked: base's credit-exposure clause holds an agreement when open orders reach the open-order
  multiple of the credit limit - the one open order stood at 5700.00 against a 65000.00 limit doubled, so no hold is
  owed, and after the cancellation no order stands accepted and unserved at all. Base's late-charge clause is raised
  when a bill is chased and is not lit by the seed. The agreement carries no cache field other than
  receivable_balance_usd, which is seeded exactly equal to the ledger sum, so this task designs no cache trap.

PERSONA. Dermot Ingalls is written relaxed and faintly amused, the opposite register to task 0's brisk Marla. What he
volunteers: the company, that the dinner on the twentieth is off, that whatever pulling it carries should go on the
account this morning, and that he is not asking for a quotation. What he gives only when asked: the direct line
3125806412, then the client account code CA-22853, with an explicit refusal to go hunting for the postcode or the
opening date unless pressed. What he reacts to, and only after the agent has said it: a request that he do something
himself (he is willing, and says it should be recorded as coming through his named account manager and that he did
not use the ordering portal, which is what fixes the
channel recorded against the instruction), a figure read to him (he does not test it and asks for it to go on the
statement), and the charge having been raised (he thanks the agent and rings off). He never states an amount, never
names a reference, and never suggests anything has to be done first. His last reaction answers the last gold action.

DIFFICULTY IN DEPTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (put what pulling it costs on the account) -> the charge policy's
own prerequisite sentence -> the records show no cancellation entry against the order -> the registration policy is the
only write that produces one, and the charter reserves it to the client -> the value that registration must carry is
itself four rules deep -> only then is the charge computable, on the entry the client's write produced. Breadth: the
charge alone turns in parallel on the channel the instruction came through, the span between two dates, the agreement's
unsettled balance, two different windows over two different event types, and a delivery count measured against the
service level's minimum order value.

EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Charging on the 6400.00 the order was quoted at: the composition rule
works from the entries the order carries. Repricing to 30 guests because the count was reduced: the reduction of
6.25 per cent is inside the band the agreement has earned, so the amendment entry's own value stands. Taking no
trading discount, which is what the computation document alone yields: the agreement's three deliveries in six months
put it on the written 6.50 rather than on the printed 5.00 or on none. Reading the value as the 5700.00 the amendment
left standing: the composition rule takes the trading discount and the programme concession off it first, and the base
sentence that would have stopped at 5700.00 is named in this policy's overwrite. Counting the notice the ordinary way,
from the day notice was given: 48 hours falls inside the free window and carries the within-notice 65 per cent, where
the account manager's count of 72 hours carries none. Reading the notice as free and stopping there: three cancellation charges stand inside the counting window, so the rate charged is half the
within-notice percentage even though the notice itself carries none. Counting those charges over three months: an
amount stands unsettled, which puts the window at twelve. Forgetting the rebate: the delivery record earns fifteen per
cent off the charge.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by the company name; verify on the telephone number and the client account code;
read the agreement (Executive Hospitality Catering Account, active, written discount 6.50, delivery site CS-271,
client account code CA-22853, unsettled 17812.50); read the order history; read the banquet agreement billing under
that same account code. Identify CO-726310 as the only
order still ahead with neither a delivery nor a cancellation entry. Work the value standing on it: band 7.5,
reduction 6.25, so the amendment entry's 5700.00 stands; discount 6.5; concession 4.0; total 10.5; standing value
5101.50. Hand the registration to the client with that figure and the guest count of 30, and let him run it
himself, recorded as coming through his named account manager. Then work the charge on the entry he produced: notice counted at 72.0 hours, which is free; twelve-month
window because an amount stands unsettled; three charges inside it and four cancellations registered, so the rate is
32.5; 1657.99 gross; fifteen per cent rebate; 1409.29. Raise it.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. Both computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator
(skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py, build_env and eval_compute) on the handling-time world of each
step - the standing value on the opening ledger, the charge on the ledger after the client's registration had been
replayed with the real tools. Outputs: standing value 5101.50 over 20 bindings and 13 branches, reconciling 15 history
rows; charge 1409.29 over 16 bindings and 11 branches, reconciling 13 history rows. Per-factor baseline substitution on
the registration gave 5728.00, 5370.00, 5472.00 and 5329.50; every factor at baseline at once gave 6400.00. On the charge it gave
2818.57, 2818.57, 0.00, 0.00 and 1657.99; all at once gave 3315.97. Prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the registration gave
1160.25. Every figure differs from the gold it belongs to, and each is recorded in computations[] where the gate
recomputes it.

RULE AND COMPUTE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Forward: compute_basis quotes a rule sentence verbatim for every binding that reads
the world or makes a choice - on the registration policy the placement and amendment reads, the tenure span, the
delivery counts, the band ladder, the reduction, the amendment lead span, the selection ladder, the discount ladder,
the two banquet reads, the concession ladder and the composition; on the charge policy the four cancellation-entry
reads, the day span, the counting ladder, the rate band, the unsettled read, the payment count, the window ladder, the
registered count, the rate ladder, the delivery count, the rebate ladder and the composition. Reverse: every
load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding. Sensitive words cross-checked: "the twelve months ending on
the day notice is given" against within_months=12, "the six months" against within_months=6, "the three months" against
within_months=3, "the higher of" against MX, "rounded to two decimal places" against each RND. The semantics that could
be read two ways are pinned: the discount taken and the programme concession are added into one total rate and act once
on the selected value rather than successively; the rate charged acts on the value the cancellation entry carries and
is rounded before the rebate is taken, and the result rounded again; the notice is counted at twenty-four hours to the
day from the day each tier names.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. The registration step carries cancellable_state with the agreement's status and
reference and the order's own placement entry as pre-action system evidence, correlated to the action's order_reference,
and its stage fact is performed by the tool itself against entries already on file. The charge step carries
cancellable_state and registration_window, both correlated through the cancellation entry the preceding step produced,
cited as prior_step rather than asserted, with frozen_time on the time gate and adjacent boundary cases recorded. Every
required customer input is quoted verbatim from user_scenario. Nothing waits on an event outside the conversation: both
writes land synchronously under one frozen_time, and the client's act is performed on the call.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale
masked, and working only from the published catering rules, the tool schemas, the rows the finders return and Dermot's
actual lines: the caller wants the cost of pulling Monday's dinner put on the account; the charge rule says it is fixed
only after a cancellation entry stands against the order carrying the value the order held when notice was given; the
history shows CO-726310 with a placement and an amendment and no cancellation; the registration is the only write that
produces such an entry and the charter reserves it to the client; the standing-value rule yields 5101.50; with that entry
written the charge rule yields 1409.29. The blind pass agrees with gold on the acts, the order, the two figures, their
order and who performs each; no second reading reaches a different sequence, because the prerequisite sentence forbids
fixing the charge first and only one order on the agreement answers the caller's description.

REVISIONS.
Round 1: none - the world was laid out to the factor design, and the first handling-time evaluation of both
computations matched the figures the design intended.
Round 2, closing the source-layer audit (F-1/T1-F1, F-2/T1-F2, F-4/T1-F4, F-5/T1-F3, T1-F5, O-2, O-3).
  F-1/T1-F1. Symptom: the notice-counting ladder's fall-through ("from the day after notice was given") appeared in
  compute and in the ladder but in no sentence of the rule, and the factor's declared baseline of 48 hours contradicted
  baseline.rule, which states the ordinary count; computing from baseline.rule alone reproduced the tier actually
  taken, so the factor was decoration. Root cause: the general sentence meant to state the fall-through instead stated
  the telephone tier, so the rule stated that tier twice and the fall-through never. Change: the fall-through is now
  the ordinary count the baseline sentence states (from the day notice was given, twenty-four hours to the day), the
  written-instruction tier (email or the ordering portal, registered the next working day) is stated in the rule as a
  named tier, the factor's baseline is RND(notice_days * 24, 2), and the world was moved off the fall-through - the
  service day is Monday 2026-04-20, two days after notice, and the client records the instruction as coming through his
  named account manager, whose tier counts from the day before. Re-run: the taken tier gives 72 hours and no
  percentage; the honest baseline gives 48 hours, the within-notice 65 per cent and a charge of 2818.57 against the
  scored 1409.29, so the factor now bears weight against the baseline its own policy states. The scored values are
  unchanged at 5101.50 and 1409.29 and the edge-skip figure is unchanged at 1160.25.
  F-2/T1-F2. Symptom: catering_amendment_terms' sentence "Every amendment rewrites the order value, and the value that
  governs any later cancellation charge is the value on the order at the moment notice of cancellation is given" was
  inherited in full and read to 5700.00 where the extended composition reads to 5101.50, leaving two defensible values
  for a scored parameter and 1574.62 against 1409.29 downstream. Root cause: the twin sentence in
  catering_cancellation_charges was declared superseded and this one was not. Change: a fourth overwrite entry on this
  policy names that base policy and quotes the sentence verbatim, replaced by the composition sentence of this policy's
  own rule. Base itself is untouched. Re-run: the divergence is declared, so the base reading is retired rather than
  rivalrous; the scored value stays 5101.50.
  F-4/T1-F4. Symptom: the cross-difficulty read joined the catering delivery_site_code (CS-###) to
  banquet_agreements.venue_code (declared VN-###) and matched only because the seed wrote CS-271 into venue_code,
  against that record's own declared format. Root cause: "at the order's delivery site" was implemented as an equality
  between two disjoint identifier namespaces. Change: the join is now on client_account_code, which both records
  declare as CA- followed by five digits; the rule says "billing under the same client account code as the catering
  agreement"; the banquet row is seeded venue_code VN-318 in its own declared format. Re-run: the read returns active
  and 350 guests as before, the tier is unchanged, and forcing the cross-category reads off still moves the result, so
  the factor bears weight on a join both record contracts admit.
  F-5/T1-F3. Symptom: standing_discount_selection had three tiers but at most two outcomes, because tier 1's
  MX(written, printed) can never be a third value; struck out, the registration computation fell to three factors,
  below the floor of four. Root cause: tier 1 was a selector over the same two quantities the other tiers already
  selected individually. Change: the factor is replaced by trading_discount_applied, a parameter factor whose three
  tiers select three distinct values - the discount written onto the agreement, the discount printed against the
  service level, and no trading discount at all - with the fall-through as the baseline, and the baseline sentence
  changed to "No trading discount is taken on the value standing." Re-run: the tier taken is the written 6.50, its
  baseline gives 5472.00 against the scored 5101.50, the computation still carries four factors (two parameter, one
  method minimum satisfied), and the whole-baseline fall-back moves from 6080.00 to 6400.00, still definite and still
  different from gold.
  T1-F5. Symptom: the two boundary counterfactuals on the registration window used different anchors, so no single
  anchor produced both quoted figures. Change: both are anchored at the moment notice is given, as base's counting rule
  states - 09:15 on 2026-04-16 to 09:15 on 2026-04-18 is 48 elapsed hours and out of time; 09:15 on 2026-04-17 to
  09:15 on 2026-04-18 is exactly 24 and, the boundary being inclusive, in time.
  O-2. The registration rule's opening sentence no longer states the cross-problem order from the depended-on side; it
  says only that the value standing is worked out afresh from the entries the order carries.
  O-3. The amendment deadline test's day-to-hours conversion is now stated in the rule.
  Observations left standing, with reasons: T1-O1 (the six-month near-miss does not flip the discount tier - the
  tier-flipping near-miss in this computation is the placed-value reading of amendment_repricing_basis, and the charge
  computation carries two more); T1-O2 (the counting tier rests on the channel the cancellation entry records, which is
  a record the prerequisite write leaves, and which the charter itself treats as how the instruction reached Larkspur
  Table); T1-O3 (the customer states the business event, not the record write, and still supplies neither the order
  reference, nor the value, nor the fact that the charge waits on an entry); O-5 and O-6 (recorded by the audit as not
  red and requiring no change).
  Gate block re-run after the changes: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK,
  GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
Round 3, closing the round-2 re-audit (R2-F1, R2-O1, R2-O2).
  R2-F1. Symptom: closing F-4 moved the banquet join in the rule, the compute, the compute_basis, the
  cross_category note and the seed, but not in programme_concession_taken's own ladder, whose two tier conditions still
  read "at the order's delivery site" and "at that site". Because the same rework put the banquet agreement's venue at
  VN-318 and the order's delivery site at CS-271, the two faces then selected different tiers on this very world: the
  rule gives a four-point concession and 5101.50, the ladder falls through to none and gives 5329.50, with the charge
  1472.28 instead of 1409.29 - two defensible values for both scored parameters, and, once the KB renders each factor's
  ladder into its own document, a factor document contradicting its own hub. Root cause: a one-place-missed edit; three
  faces moved and the fourth did not. Change: both tier conditions are now taken word for word from the concession
  sentence of this policy's own rule - "the client holds a private event and banquet agreement billing under the same
  client account code as the catering agreement, that agreement stands active and the largest guest count its package
  handles reaches two hundred" and "the client holds such an agreement under that account code that stands active and
  the largest guest count its package handles falls short of two hundred" - so the hub and the factor document cannot
  diverge. Re-run: the ladder
  reading and the rule reading now select the same tier, the concession is 4.0, the scored values stay 5101.50 and
  1409.29, and the factor's baseline substitution still gives 5329.50, which is now only a counterfactual rather than a
  rival reading.
  Sweep of every other face, run mechanically rather than by eye, because a one-place-missed defect is only closed if
  all the places are checked: for all four policies, every ladder tier condition and every prose outcome was tested
  word by word against its policy's rule (no word in a tier condition or outcome is absent from the rule); every
  cross-category join key used in compute was tested against the cross_category reads list; and the registration policy
  was scanned for any surviving mention of a delivery site or a venue. The sweep found one further drift and it is
  fixed: amendment_repricing_basis's second tier condition did not carry the day-count conversion that round 2's O-3
  fix added to the rule, so it now reads "counted in whole days from the day the amendment was asked for to the service
  day and taken at twenty-four hours to the day" exactly as the rule does. Nothing else diverged; the cafe join on
  site_code is stated identically in the rule, the compute and the ladders of both task 0 policies, and both records
  declare that field in the same CS- format.
  R2-O1 (the persona's channel statement is load-bearing and the docstring offered a competing reading). Closed inside
  the write domain rather than recorded. The registration tool's order_channel gloss now asks for "the route by which
  this cancellation instruction reached Larkspur Table, which is a fact about how the client passed the instruction on
  rather than about the medium of any one conversation", reserves account_manager for an instruction given "to the
  named catering account manager looking after them rather than to the client services desk", and reserves phone for
  one the client "spoke ... to the client services desk on the telephone and passed it through no one else". An agent
  who anchors on the call being taken by telephone is now answered by the contract itself, not only by the persona.
  The argument tracing quotes the new wording and names phone as the reading to guard against. The persona is
  unchanged, and its channel sentence is load-bearing to the tune of 1409.28 on the scored value: it must survive into
  the rendered materials and the user simulator intact.
  R2-O2 (the banquet finder's docstring does not name the field the new join reads). Not closable at its source:
  share_tools.py is blueprint, base is frozen, and it is outside this write domain. Closed as far as the domain allows,
  by declaring the join key where this charter does control the record - cross_category.reads on the registration
  policy now lists client_account_code alongside status and variant_name, so the rendered materials state which field
  of the banquet agreement the concession is decided from. The value itself is reachable either way: the finder returns
  the whole row, and the catering agreement finder does advertise "the client account code it bills under", so the
  agent holds both sides of the join. The same declaration was made on the two cafe-reading policies, whose join key
  site_code was likewise undeclared.
  Gate block re-run after the round-3 changes: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK,
  COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
Round 4, closing the render-layer audit's C1 and answering its two policy-side notes.
  C1. Symptom: programme_concession_taken selected its tier on "its package is written for two hundred guests or more"
  while binding CPARAM('banquet','max_guests'). Those words are not free: the Private Event & Banquet Services schedule
  published at docs/banquet/package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad.json defines the vocabulary the other way
  round - "The smallest guest count is the guest count the package is written for and the largest is the guest count
  the package handles" - so a reader following the published corpus resolves "written for" to the Seated Banquet

user_scenario:
Dermot Ingalls looks after executive services at Halbrook Instruments Corporation, which mostly means he is the man who feeds the board and whoever the board is trying to impress. He is easy-going on the phone and faintly amused by his own weekend: the visiting delegation the dinner on the twentieth was laid on for has rearranged its trip, so the dinner on the twentieth is off, and he would like it dealt with this morning rather than left hanging over a Saturday.

He says at the start that he is ringing for Halbrook Instruments Corporation and that the executive dinner booked for Monday the twentieth will not be going ahead. He is clear about what he wants done with it: whatever pulling it carries should go on the account as a charge, this morning, so that finance sees it on the statement rather than hearing about it in a month. He is not asking for a quotation to consider, and he says so if the point is raised.

When he is asked to confirm who he is, he gives the direct line the account is under, 3125806412, and if a second detail is wanted he reads the client account code from the top of the last statement, CA-22853. He can find the billing postcode and the day the account was opened if he is pushed, but says he would rather not go hunting through the filing system for them, and if pressed he repeats the two he has already given. He does not know any internal reference numbers and says so if he is asked, telling the agent that the desk's own screen is the better source.

If the agent needs him to do something himself, he is willing, and he says it should go down as coming through Halbrook's named catering account manager, who he spoke to first thing and who he says has already had the kitchen warned; he has never got on with the ordering portal and did not use it. He asks for the exact wording and the exact figures, reads them back once, and does it. If the agent tells him what the order stood at or what it will cost, he does not test the number against anything of his own; he says finance will want it on the statement and leaves it there. He never volunteers an amount, and if he is asked what he thinks it comes to he says he genuinely has no idea and that the desk should read it off the record. Once he hears the charge has been raised on the account, he thanks the agent and rings off.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.catering_agreement_id: The internal reference of the client's one corporate catering service agreement, read from the agreement lookup at step 2 and given to the client by the agent when the action is handed over. Basis: the registration action asks for "the reference number of the corporate catering service agreement the order sits under, as the desk reads it off the client's agreement record"; the caller has none of his own ("He does not know any internal reference numbers and says so if he is asked"). Uniqueness: the client holds exactly one catering agreement, so only one reference can be passed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The internal reference of the client organisation profile returned by the profile lookup at step 0 for the company the caller names. Basis: the profile lookup returns "A single matching profile" in full for the stated organisation name. Uniqueness: exactly one profile carries that organisation name, and the agreement read at step 2 carries the same client reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.order_reference: CO-726310. Basis: the order history read at step 3 carries a placement entry and an amendment entry with that order reference for service on 2026-04-20, which is the dinner the caller says "will not be going ahead". Uniqueness: it is the only order on the agreement whose service day is still ahead of 2026-04-18 and which carries neither a delivery entry nor a cancellation entry, so no other reference answers the caller's request.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_date: 2026-04-20. Basis: both the placement entry and the amendment entry for CO-726310 record the service day as 2026-04-20, and the registration action asks for "the day the catering was to have been served". Uniqueness: no other service day is recorded against that order reference, and the caller names the same day as Monday the twentieth.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.headcount: 30. Basis: the amendment entry of 2026-04-10 on CO-726310 records the guest count as 30, and the registration action asks for "the guest count the order stood on when it was pulled". Uniqueness: the placement entry's 32 was superseded by that amendment, which is the last entry on the order before notice, so the count standing is 30 and no other figure is recorded.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.order_channel: account_manager. Basis: the registration action's own contract asks for "the route by which this cancellation instruction reached Larkspur Table, which is a fact about how the client passed the instruction on rather than about the medium of any one conversation", and to pass "account_manager when the client gave the instruction to the named catering account manager looking after them rather than to the client services desk"; the caller says the cancellation "should go down as coming through Halbrook's named catering account manager, who he spoke to first thing and who he says has already had the kitchen warned". Uniqueness: online_portal does not hold because "he has never got on with the ordering portal and did not use it"; email does not hold because nothing was sent in writing; phone is the reading to guard against, since the client is on the telephone to the desk while the action runs, and it is excluded by the contract's own words - it asks for the route the instruction took and reserves phone for an instruction the client "passed through no one else", whereas this one went through the account manager first thing, who had already warned the kitchen.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.standing_order_value_usd: 5101.50. The order was placed at 6400.00 on a guest count of 32, and the amendment entry of 2026-04-10 records 5700.00 on a guest count of 30, a reduction of 6.25 per cent. The agreement has run 16 months, at least a year but less than two, and carried 5 deliveries in the twelve months ending 2026-04-18, three or more, so the free reduction band standing on the order is one and a half times the 5.00 printed against the Executive Hospitality Catering Account, 7.5. The reduction of 6.25 per cent is no more than that band, so the value the most recent amendment entry records stands: 5700.00. The agreement carried 3 deliveries in the six months ending that day, three or more, so the trading discount taken is the 6.5 written onto the agreement rather than the 5.00 printed against the service level. The client holds a Seated Banquet Package billing under CA-22853, the same client account code as the catering agreement, that stands active and whose package handles 350 guests at most, two hundred or more, so a programme concession of 4.0 points is taken. The two are added into one total concession rate of 10.5 and the selected value is reduced once by it: 5101.50.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_date: 2026-04-20. argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_charge_usd: 1409.29. The cancellation entry standing against the order carries 5101.50 and records notice given on 2026-04-18 for service on 2026-04-20, two days later, through the client's named account manager. The notice therefore counts from the day before notice was given, 72.0 hours, which reaches the 72 free-cancellation hours printed against the Executive Hospitality Catering Account, so the notice given yields no percentage at all. An amount stands unsettled on the agreement, 17812.50, so the cancellation charges already raised are counted over the twelve months ending 2026-04-18: 3 of them, on 2025-07-15, 2025-10-21 and 2026-01-16. That is at least two and fewer than four, and 4 cancellations were registered on the agreement in those twelve months, so the rate charged is the higher of the percentage the notice yields, none, and half the 65.00 within-notice percentage, 32.5. Applied to 5101.50 that gives 1657.99. The agreement carried 5 deliveries in the twelve months ending that day, at least three and fewer than six, and 5101.50 reaches the 2400.00 minimum order value printed against the service level, so a rebate of 15.0 per cent is allowed and the charge becomes 1409.29.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-04-18 the order CO-726310 carries a placement entry of 2026-03-28 and an amendment entry of 2026-04-10 and nothing else; no cancellation entry anywhere in the agreement's history quotes that order reference, and the most recent cancellation entry on the agreement belongs to CO-723488 and was registered on 2026-01-16.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The client's own registration writes a cancellation entry for 5101.50 against CO-726310 posted 2026-04-18, which then becomes the most recent cancellation entry on the agreement and is what the charge reads for its value, its notice day, its service day and its channel.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has one edge and therefore one topological order: the cancellation entry must stand before the charge is fixed. There are no parallel prerequisites to commute. The reverse order is not merely unordered but arithmetically different, because the charge reads the value, the notice day, the service day and the channel off the most recent cancellation entry, and without the client's registration those four are read off a cancellation registered on 2026-01-16 instead.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying with the client's registration skipped and everything else unchanged, the charge computes to 1160.25 instead of 1409.29: the value read falls from 5101.50 to 4200.00, the notice day and service day become 2026-01-16 and 2026-01-28, and the count of cancellations registered in the twelve months falls from 4 to 3.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a cancellation entry, a record to be written first, or that the client must act in person before the charge can be worked out. Dermot says only that the dinner on the twentieth is off, that whatever pulling it carries should go on the account this morning, and, in a passive branch that fires only after the agent has asked him to do something, that he is willing and that it should be recorded as coming through his named account manager rather than the ordering portal. He names no order reference, no value and no step, and he never suggests that anything has to happen before the charge can be raised.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_cancellation_charge_b7aa0639 in task_tools.py builds its row id, writes one catering_orders charge entry and updates the agreement's balance from the figure it is given; it reads the order history for nothing, makes no test of whether a cancellation entry stands against the order, and returns its confirmation whatever the ledger holds. Called before the client's registration it would still write, and would simply write a charge worked out on the wrong entry. Likewise register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0 writes its cancellation entry without asking whether the order was already served, already cancelled, or still inside any window.

factor_trace: amendment_repricing_basis (method): the order was placed at 6400.00 on 32 guests and the amendment entry of 2026-04-10 records 5700.00 on 30 guests, a reduction of 6.25 per cent, which is no more than the 7.5 per cent free reduction band standing on the order, so the first tier applies and the value the most recent amendment entry records stands, 5700.00; the baseline lets the value the order was placed at stand, which would have given 5728.00.

free_reduction_band_standing (parameter): the agreement has run 16 months, at least a year but less than two, and carried 5 deliveries in the twelve months ending 2026-04-18, three or more, so the second tier applies and the band standing is one and a half times the 5.00 printed against the service level, 7.5; the baseline uses the printed 5.00, under which the 6.25 per cent reduction would be beyond the band and the order repriced to the amended count, giving 5370.00.

trading_discount_applied (parameter): the agreement carried 3 deliveries in the six months ending 2026-04-18, three or more, so the first tier applies and the trading discount taken is the 6.5 written onto the agreement; the baseline takes no trading discount at all, which would have given 5472.00.

programme_concession_taken (parameter, cross-difficulty): the client holds a Seated Banquet Package billing under CA-22853, the same client account code as the catering agreement, which stands active and whose package handles 350 guests at most, two hundred or more, so the first tier applies and a programme concession of 4.0 points is taken; the baseline takes none, which would have given 5329.50.

Bindings outside every factor: placed_value, placed_headcount and service_day read 6400.00, 32 and 2026-04-20 off the placement entry; amendment_count, amended_value, amended_headcount and amendment_notice_day read the single amendment entry; total_concession_pct adds the discount taken and the programme concession into one rate of 10.5; result reduces the selected value once by that rate and rounds at the end.

factor_trace: notice_counting_basis (method): the cancellation entry records the channel as the client's named account manager, so the first tier applies and the notice given is counted from the day before notice was given to the service day, 2 days plus one at twenty-four hours to the day, 72.0 hours; the baseline is the ordinary count from the day notice was given, 48 hours, which falls short of the 72 free-cancellation hours and so carries the within-notice percentage, giving 2818.57.

notice_band_rate (parameter): notice was given on 2026-04-18 for service on 2026-04-20, so not on the service day itself, and the 72.0 hours counted reach the 72 free-cancellation hours printed against the Executive Hospitality Catering Account, so the second tier applies and the notice given yields no percentage at all; the baseline yields the 65.00 within-notice percentage, which would have given 2818.57.

cancellation_counting_window (method): 17812.50 stands unsettled on the agreement, so the first tier applies and the cancellation charges already raised are counted over the twelve months ending 2026-04-18, 3 of them; the baseline counts over the three months ending that day, which finds none and would have given 0.00.

repeat_cancellation_rate_basis (method): 3 cancellation charges stand raised inside the counting window, at least two and fewer than four, and 4 cancellations were registered on the agreement in the twelve months ending 2026-04-18, so the second tier applies and the rate charged is the higher of the percentage the notice yields, none, and half the 65.00 within-notice percentage, 32.5; the baseline charges the percentage the notice yields, which would have given 0.00.

delivery_record_rebate (parameter): the agreement carried 5 deliveries in the twelve months ending 2026-04-18, at least three and fewer than six, and the 5101.50 the cancellation entry carries reaches the 2400.00 minimum order value printed against the service level, so the second tier applies and a rebate of 15.0 per cent is allowed; the baseline allows none, which would have given 1657.99.

Bindings outside every factor: cancelled_value reads 5101.50 off the cancellation entry the client registered at the preceding step; unsettled reads 17812.50 off the agreement; gross_charge applies the rate charged to the value the cancellation entry carries and rounds; result takes the rebate off that charge and rounds again.
